name: Integrated Scheme for Export Promotion & Quality Improvement in Spices and Research and Development of Cardamom: Post-Harvest Improvement: Nutmeg /clove drier (nos )
brief: The Integrated Scheme for Export Promotion & Quality Improvement in Spices and Research and Development of Cardamom: Post-Harvest Improvement – Mechanical Dryers for Nutmeg and Clove is implemented by the Spices Board, India…
briefFull: The Integrated Scheme for Export Promotion & Quality Improvement in Spices and Research and Development of Cardamom: Post-Harvest Improvement – Mechanical Dryers for Nutmeg and Clove is implemented by the Spices Board, India, under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India.
details: The Integrated Scheme for Export Promotion & Quality Improvement in Spices and Research and Development of Cardamom: Post-Harvest Improvement – Mechanical Dryers for Nutmeg and Clove is implemented by the Spices Board, India, under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India. The scheme aims to promote the hygienic drying of nutmeg and clove using mechanical dryers among farmers. This helps in producing high-quality nutmeg, mace, and clove, improving product quality and enhancing their export potential. The scheme is being implemented in accordance with the modalities and guidelines approved by the Competent Authority under the Integrated Scheme for Export Promotion & Quality Improvement in Spices and Research and Development of Cardamom during the 15th Finance Commission period (2021–22 to 2025–26).
benefits:
- 50 % of cost of unit, subject to a maximum of ₹ 37,500/- per unit for General Category and 75% subject to maximum of ₹ 56,000/- per unit for NE/SC/ST & 90% Spice Producer's Groups in Identified Clusters subject to maximum ₹67,500/-
- Individual growers having a minimum of 0.10 ha [20 nos. nutmeg/clove trees] and up to 8 ha [1600 nos. nutmeg/clove tress
- Assistance for groups/FPOs will be as in QGBG.
eligibility:
1.All spice growing states and regions in India/UT.
2. Designated Officials will conduct final inspection and recommend the eligible cases. Since it is a multipurpose drier the facility can be used for drying other suitable spices also and for availing assistance necessary approval may be taken from Director(Dev.) Spices Board with recommendation of Regional Officer.
howToApply:
[Online]
**Registration**
Step 1: The applicant should visit the [ServicesPlus](https://serviceonline.gov.in/dbt/) website.
Step 2: Click on the “[Register” ](https://serviceonline.gov.in/dbt/citizenRegistration.html)option on the homepage.
Step 3: Fill out the registration form by entering Full Name, Email ID, Mobile Number, Password, selecting State, and Captcha.
Step 4: Review all details carefully and submit the registration form.
Step 5: An OTP will be sent to your registered mobile number or email; enter the OTP and click “Verify.”
Step 6: Registration will be completed successfully, and a confirmation message will be displayed or sent via email.
**Login**
Step 1: The applicant should visit the ServicesPlus website and click on [“Login.”](https://serviceonline.gov.in/dbt/loginWindow.do)
Step 2: Enter your Email ID, Password, and Captcha.
Step 3: Select the relevant service/scheme name.
Step 4: Fill in the required details in the application form.
Step 5: Submit the application.
documentsRequired:
a) Land documents of ownership / legal possession
b) Current year land tax paid receipt / Chitta Adangal
c) Aadhar card
d) Bank pass book first page
e) Invoice and payment documents towards purchase from valid manufacturer of the equipment/device empaneled by Spices Board

faqs.q: What is the objective of the Nutmeg/Clove Drier scheme?
faqs.a: The scheme aims to promote the hygienic drying of nutmeg and clove using mechanical dryers. This helps farmers produce high-quality nutmeg, mace, and clove, thereby improving their market value and export potential.

faqs.q: Who is eligible to apply for assistance under this scheme?
faqs.a: Individual nutmeg and clove growers having a minimum holding of 0.10 hectare with at least 20 nutmeg or clove trees and up to 8 hectares with a maximum of 1,600 trees are eligible to apply. Farmer groups and Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) may also avail assistance under the scheme.

faqs.q: What financial assistance is available for General Category beneficiaries?
faqs.a: General Category beneficiaries are eligible for assistance equal to 50% of the cost of the drier unit, subject to a maximum of ₹37,500 per unit.

faqs.q: What financial assistance is available for NE, SC, and ST beneficiaries?
faqs.a: Beneficiaries belonging to the North-Eastern Region, Scheduled Castes, and Scheduled Tribes are eligible for assistance equal to 75% of the cost of the unit, subject to a maximum of ₹56,000 per unit.

faqs.q: What assistance is available for Spice Producers' Groups in identified clusters?
faqs.a: Spice Producers' Groups operating in identified clusters can receive assistance equal to 90% of the cost of the drier unit, subject to a maximum of ₹67,500 per unit.

faqs.q: Is Aadhaar mandatory for availing the benefit?
faqs.a: Yes. Aadhaar is a mandatory document required for identity verification and processing of the application.

faqs.q: Can farmer groups and FPOs apply under this scheme?
faqs.a: Yes. Farmer groups and FPOs are eligible to receive assistance under the provisions applicable to group beneficiaries as prescribed in the scheme guidelines.

faqs.q: Can assistance be claimed for equipment purchased from any manufacturer?
faqs.a: No. The equipment must be purchased from a valid manufacturer empanelled by the Spices Board, and supporting invoices and payment documents must be submitted.
